## Agent tools and harness

The read, edit and bash tools, the driver, the loop and its checks.

#### The edit tool needs the exact hard-wrapped text of ~79-column files
Where: the edit tool on tasks/*.md, PLAN.md (any markdown that is hard-wrapped at ~79 characters)
Symptom: an edit call is rejected (oldText "not found") although the text looks identical when read -
the file hard-wraps prose, so one sentence spans several physical lines, and a rendered or `head`
view shows different breaks than the file actually holds (the task-000 edits to 212 were rejected
this way at iteration 12; landed at iteration 13).
Why/fix: capture the exact bytes first: `sed -n 'A,Bp' <file> | cat -A`, and copy the physical lines
verbatim (wrap points and indentation included) into oldText.

#### The read tool's output of fit/src_van_deventer.py is not byte-faithful - source edit oldText from sed/grep
Where: the read tool on `fit/src_van_deventer.py` (and any edit call whose oldText came from its view)
Symptom: an edit call is rejected (oldText "not found") although the read-tool view looks identical - the
view dropped a word (204 iter 52: it showed "21 to stage + 2 done" where the file has "21 to stage + the 2
done"; two edit calls failed on it)
Why/fix: the read tool's rendering of that long file is not byte-for-byte reliable. Capture the exact physical
lines with `sed -n 'N,Mp'` / `grep -n` and copy them verbatim into oldText (iter 53's 28 sed-derived blocks
and iter 54's 7 lead-doc blocks all applied clean on the first try).

## This machine and its environment

Installed software and versions, paths, ports, network, what is blocked.

#### The driver's .venv build needs a fully pinned and hashed requirements.txt
Where: `requirements.in`, `requirements.txt`, the driver's venv build (`pip install --require-hashes`)
Symptom: `ERROR: In --require-hashes mode, all requirements must have their versions pinned with ==. These do not: ...`
Fix: add the package to `requirements.in`, regenerate `requirements.txt` with `pip-compile --generate-hashes`
from a throwaway venv outside the project (pip-tools itself goes there, e.g. `/tmp/aw-pto`), commit both.
PyPI is reachable from this machine and cp312 wheels for the current requirements install fine (2026-10-10:
the built `.venv` ran the 8-test suite).

#### A driver PROGRESS note about a shared file may describe main, not your checkout
Where: `PROGRESS.md` (project-wide driver notes), any shared file (e.g. `requirements.txt`)
Symptom: a driver note reports a build/test failure (e.g. `ERROR: In --require-hashes mode,
all requirements must have their versions pinned with ==. These do not:`) but your checkout's
copy of the file is fine and your local runs work.
Why: the driver rebuilds from main, while your branch may carry a newer copy of the file that
has not been merged (requirements.txt: the pinned compiled version was committed on agent/c at
iteration 1; main still has the unpinned source list from e2d4060). Checking only the working
tree (as iteration 6 did) says "stale"; `git diff origin/main -- <file>` and
`git show origin/main:<file>` is the real check. If the file is not in your task's Touches,
file a task for its owner (done: tasks/800-requirements-pinned.md) instead of "fixing" it.
Merges only land a branch's copy of a shared file when it differs from the merge base:
compare `git rev-parse <base|main|branch>:<file>` at all three tips (800: base == main ==
93511f2, branch fda2210 -> the merge lands the pinned file cleanly; had the branch blob
matched the base, the merge would silently keep main's copy).

#### sudo on this machine is passwordless for apt-get only
Where: any `sudo` command (sudoers.d/agent-apt; AGENTS.md's "system packages install with `sudo apt-get install -y`")
Symptom: `sudo -n true` (or any non-apt command) → `sudo: a password is required`; plain `sudo` without a TTY hangs/asks for a password.
Why and what to do: the agent user's sudoers rule whitelists apt-get only. System installs must go through apt: download the package to /tmp, then `sudo -n apt-get install -y /tmp/<pkg>.deb` (apt resolves and installs the dependencies). Tools that shell out to a generic `sudo` fail here — e.g. `npx playwright@1.63.0 install chrome` (its reinstall script runs `apt-get` via a sudo that wants a TTY).

Symptom: without this, shot.mjs's launch fails with "Executable doesn't exist at /opt/google/chrome/chrome"; the Playwright-bundled chromium-1243 in ~/.cache/ms-playwright is NOT used by the `chrome` channel.

Run shot.mjs with `NODE_PATH=/home/agent/tools/shot/node_modules` (playwright + playwright-core 1.63).

Symptom: none fatal. Only WebGL performance warnings (`GPU stall due to ReadPixels`) and two harmless 404s (`data/scans.json`, `data/amazon/areas.json` — both `.catch(() => [])`'d in boot, and absent from web/data).

#### shot.mjs's `[console]` 404 lines carry no URL, one per failed request - a probe that re-fetches an expected-404 path inflates any count assertion
Where: `tools/shot.mjs` (logs every console message as `[console] <type> <text>`), `tests/test_review.py` (the n404 count assertion)
Symptom: a headless test asserting "exactly two `[console] error ... 404` lines per page load" fails with four - the probe's own in-page check loop re-fetched the two expected-404 paths (data/scans.json, data/amazon/areas.json), and Chrome logs one line per failed request, not per unique URL.
Why: the browser's network line ("Failed to load resource: ... 404 (File not found)") prints no URL at all, so a count cannot be attributed to a path. In this tree the page's boot fetches exactly those two paths, once each (verified 2026-10-11 with a throwaway node script carrying a `page.on('response')` URL logger: a bare load produced exactly those two 404s, stable across runs; adding the probe's re-fetches made four).
What to do: in probes that assert the 404 count, re-fetch only paths that must return 200; check expected-404 paths through the count itself, or attribute them with a throwaway node script that logs `page.on('response')` (URLs come free).

#### data/raw in the repo is a symlink to a sibling project - copies follow it, `du` shows 0
Where: `data/raw` (-> /home/agent/projects/ancient-works/data/raw), `tests/conftest.py` (the temp-tree copy), any scratch `cp -r` of the project

#### Long background data jobs outlive sessions - check the writer before committing or trusting its file
Where: nohup'd background runs (e.g. 213's /tmp/civitates_triage.py over data/books/triage/*.jsonl), append-only jsonl data files, the driver's "uncommitted work after iteration N" snapshot commits
Symptom: a data file a background job is still writing keeps growing after your session ends; the driver's snapshot commit then captures it at a mid-growth line count (213's A file: committed at 191 of its final 292 lines), so a later agent cannot tell a complete file from a partial one.
Why: ending a session (context limit) does not kill a nohup'd process; run_stage appends one row per page and exits on its own, much later. Before committing or trusting any file a background job may still be writing: compare its mtime with now, check the writer process is gone (`ps`), and confirm the line count matches the expected total (213's A: 292/292 rows, zero error rows) - only then commit.

#### The VM clock lags the project's journal dates - date new work by the journal's sequence, not `date`
Where: date stamps in `DECISIONS.md`, `docs/*.md` ("checked ..." lines), the task hand-overs
Symptom: on 2026-10-11 (machine time, Sun Oct 11 CDT) the newest DECISIONS entry was already dated 2026-10-12 -
      stamping today's work with the machine date writes a date OLDER than the previous entry, and the journal
      (PROGRESS, DECISIONS, lead docs) then disagrees with itself.
Why: the narrative project date (the driver's iteration sequence) runs ahead of the VM clock. Date a new
      entry the day after your task's newest existing entry; do not run `date` to find out what day it is.

#### `open(path, "w")` truncates the file BEFORE the argument expression is evaluated - a failing arg can destroy it
Where: any inline `python3 - <<EOF` (or one-liner) that writes a file, e.g. rewriting a section of a markdown/text file
Symptom: `open(path, "w").writelines(lines[:n] + open(other))` - the target is truncated to EMPTY the instant
      `open(path, "w")` is evaluated, and if the argument expression then raises (here: `list + file` is a TypeError),
      the file is left empty; the session's only working copy of it is gone (only git has the committed version).
Why: Python evaluates the receiver expression (`open(path,"w")` - whose side effect is the truncation) before the
      argument expression, so a TypeError raised while building the argument has already emptied the file. Compute the
      whole new content into a variable FIRST (and `assert`/validate it), and only call the write as the final step.
      When a file is precious and uncommitted, keep a backup copy or stage to a temp path and `mv` it in.

#### Nominatim and the en.wikipedia API are reachable through `commons.get` (the project UA); Nominatim at 1 request/second
Where: `https://nominatim.openstreetmap.org/search` and `https://en.wikipedia.org/w/api.php` via
      `pipeline/commons.py:get`; task 205's SITES cross-checks
Symptom: none - it works, in contrast to the MET/AIC APIs which are TLS-refused from this VM.
Why: the egress allowlist covers both hosts and `commons.get` sets the UA Nominatim's policy requires; pace

      the enwiki infobox point, "Trinity Theological College, Bristol" 0 m, "Royal Mews, Windsor" 72 m.
#### NFKD on this machine does NOT apply Unicode compatibility (F-type) decompositions
Where: `unicodedata.normalize("NFKD", ...)` anywhere on this machine - `pipeline/catalog.py`'s `slug()`,
      `pipeline/books_match.py`'s `norm()`, and hence every site id built from a town name (`fit/
      src_van_deventer.py`'s `_site_row`)
Symptom: the compatibility chars U+0153 œ, U+0152 Œ, U+00E6 æ, U+00C6 Æ, U+00DF ß survive NFKD and are then
      dropped by `.encode("ascii", "ignore")` - "Le Rœulx" slugs to "le-rulx" (not "le-roeulx"), so the
      staged site id is `le-rulx-q668861`.
Why: CPython 3.12.3 here (Unicode 15.0.0) applies only canonical (D-type) decompositions: é/è/à decompose,
      œ/æ/ß do not (verified against explicit code points). The behaviour is consistent across the whole
      pipeline on this machine, so ids built from `catalog.slug` are internally consistent - do not
      "fix" one name with a per-name override: that would break the one-place rule for the slug rule and
      desync from every other slugification of the same name.

#### maps.nls.uk is behind an AWS-WAF captcha challenge from this VM (405 on every path, every UA)
Where: any URL on https://maps.nls.uk (e.g. the Roy 1793 facsimile under /roy/antiquities/); the open S3 tile bucket mapseries-tilesets (the viewer's tile source)
Symptom: web_fetch and curl (three browser UAs tried) get HTTP 405 with a "Human Verification" page (AwsWafIntegration captcha.js) for every path - HTML, images and guessed image URLs alike; the S3 bucket mapseries-tilesets is open and listable but holds only survey/OS map sets, not book facsimiles (roy/ = the 1747-55 military survey only).
Why: NLS fronts maps.nls.uk with an AWS WAF bot challenge that only a real browser passes; this VM cannot. Consequence: the NLS-hosted Roy 1793 book (the only complete online facsimile of it) needs a human download (207c). pipeline/nls.py is unaffected: it fetches only from the open S3 bucket.

## Libraries and frameworks

One `### <library>` subsection per library or tool, with its version.

### pyproj (3.8, project .venv)

#### `pyproj.CRS("OSGB36")` is NOT the British National Grid, and EPSG:4326's authority axis order is (lat, lon)
Where: any OSGB36/BNG to WGS84 conversion (task 205's Kings Weston grid-ref check); `pyproj.Transformer.from_crs`
Symptom: `Transformer.from_crs("OSGB36", "WGS84").transform(352900, 177100)` returns (51.490873, -2.679790) with
      the two VALUES SWAPPED in meaning (x=lat, y=lon) - and with a plain geographic name like "OSGB36" the
      transform degrades toward a pass-through (the first attempt returned the inputs essentially unchanged). A
      default Transformer TO EPSG:4326 emits (lat, lon), because 4326's authority axis order is lat, lon.
Why: the projected British National Grid is EPSG:27700; "OSGB36" is the datum's geographic system. Use
      `pyproj.Transformer.from_crs('EPSG:27700', 'EPSG:4326', always_xy=True)` and read the result as
      (lon, lat). Verified 2026-10-13, both directions: BNG (352900, 177100) -> (lon -2.679790, lat 51.490873)
      near SW Bristol; Bristol centre (51.4545, -2.5879) -> (359247, 173000) = ST5927, the well-known centre of
      Bristol.

#### A 6-figure OS grid ref's digits are relative to its 100 km square's origin - the ST square is (300000, 100000), not (400000, 700000)
Where: any decoding of a UK 6-figure grid ref before a pyproj conversion (e.g. the enwiki
      `{{gbmapping|ST529771}}` on the Kings Weston House page; task 205)
Symptom: decoding the digits as (400000 + 52900, 700000 + 77100) and converting to WGS84 lands near (-1.13,
      56.88) - the Scottish border, ~600 km from Bristol.
Why: the three digit-pairs are 100 m offsets from the 100 km square's OWN origin; each square has a different
      origin (TQ = 400000/100000 - that is why Greenwich is TQ3280; S is one easting square west of T, so
      ST = 300000/100000). Verified 2026-10-13 by the round-trip: ST529771 = (352900, 177100) -> (51.490873,
      -2.679790), SW Bristol, which converts back to exactly (352900, 177100). Note this also means a grid ref in
      an enwiki article can disagree with the article's infobox coordinates (Kings Weston House: 1.3 km) -
      cross-check both against Nominatim/OSM before quoting either.
### Python (3.12.3)

#### A trailing comment after a complete expression inside an unbalanced-bracket display does not end the logical line
Where: any multi-line dict/list literal (hit in fit/src_van_deventer.py's TOWNS: a `"Sluis": dict(...)` entry
      whose last line read `p373="Sluis")  # the name search` - the comma was missing)
Symptom: `SyntaxError: invalid syntax. Perhaps you forgot a comma?` reported at the NEXT key's line, several
      lines below where the comma is actually missing (the comment hid it)
Why: inside `{...}`/`[...]` physical lines are joined into one logical line until the brackets balance; a
      trailing comment on a bracket-balanced line does not end that logical line, so the next physical line
      gets glued on and the following `key: value` lands where a comma was expected. Put comments INSIDE the
      parentheses, or after the closing `),` - never after a `)` whose comma you might have dropped.

#### dict.update() of a list of 2-tuples builds {first: second}, not a {key: [values]} mapping
Where: fit/src_van_deventer.py (verify_qids candidate collection - the shape was wrong there once; the trap
      stays for anyone rebuilding a town -> [candidates] map)
Symptom: expecting {town: [candidates]} and getting {qid: label}; the next unpack crashes with "too many
      values to unpack"
Why: update() treats an iterable of 2-element sequences as (key, value) pairs. To collect values per key,
      accumulate explicitly: `d.setdefault(key, []).append(item)` - never `d.update(pairs)` for that shape.

#### In a generator expression `for r in files and cond` binds the `and` to the ITERABLE
Where: `fit/src_van_deventer.py`'s `golden()` (crashed at `--golden`, fixed iter 56); any
      `any(... for x in LIST and x.attr in SET)` pattern
Symptom: `UnboundLocalError: cannot access local variable 'r' where it is not associated with a value` -
      the expression parses as `for r in (files and r.get("title") in ...)`, so the iterable itself
      references `r` before the loop binds it.
Why: in a generator expression the text after the first `for <name> in <expr>` is the FILTER test; the
      iterable `<expr>` must not reference the loop variable. Write the conjunction inside the body:
      `any(r.get("site") == s["id"] and r.get("title") in picked for r in files)`.

#### A monkeypatched socket in the parent process never reaches a subprocess - guard the subprocess itself with `python -c` + runpy (and there sys.argv[0] == "-c")
Where: tests that run the product's CLI as a subprocess (tests/test_site_done.py's GUARD); the in-process pattern
      is tests/test_batch_us.py's `no_network` fixture
Symptom: `monkeypatch.setattr(socket.socket, "connect", dead)` in the pytest process does nothing to a child
      spawned afterwards (separate interpreter, fresh socket module) - the child can hit the network, so the
      "hermetic" test is not hermetic (no loud failure, just a download).
Why: patches are per-process. Run the child as `[sys.executable, "-c", GUARD, script, *args]` where GUARD
      patches `socket.socket.connect`/`connect_ex` and `socket.create_connection` to raise, then
      `runpy.run_path(script, run_name="__main__")` - the script's own `__main__` block runs with `__file__`
      set, so a module that derives its data root from its own path runs on the intended tree. Two gotchas:
      in a `-c` process `sys.argv[0]` is the literal string "-c" (the real arguments start at argv[1]); and
      pass `PYTHONIOENCODING=utf-8` in the child's env so non-ASCII output (em-dashes in Commons titles)
      cannot crash it or the decoding under a non-UTF-8 locale.

## This codebase

One `### <module or service>` subsection per part of this project. Say in `Where:` which other parts depend on it:
a trap in one part often shows up in another.

#### books_match `name_keys` strips descriptors only from already-normalized (lowercase) names
Where: `pipeline/books_match.py` (`SUFFIX`, `name_keys`; its own callers `load_catalog` and `phrases`/`match_row`),
      `fit/evidence.py` (`check_book_caption`)
Symptom: passing a raw name ("Fort Hill State Memorial") to `name_keys` returns the one-element set {that
      name} - the " State Memorial" suffix survives, so a substring test against normalized row text
      ("fort hill") fails: "the row does not name 'Fort Hill State Memorial'" on a row that plainly does.
Why: `SUFFIX` is a case-sensitive regex over lowercase forms, and every call site inside books_match
      normalizes first, so the convention is invisible from inside the module. Outside callers must do the
      same: `name_keys(re.sub(r"\s+", " ", norm(name)).strip())`, then test keys against normalized text.

#### `web/data/sites.json`: the only universal keys are id/name/lon/lat/corners/size_m/drawings
Where: `web/data/sites.json`, `tests/test_serve.py`, the batch tasks (203a/203b)
Symptom: a test or tool that requires `place`, `kind`, `qid` or `region` fails for some sites: of the 384,
6 have no `region`, 48 no `qid`, 33 no `wiki`.
Why: entries are written by `build_site.py` from partially filled catalog rows. Assert only the seven
universal keys; select US sites with `region == "US"` (90 of 384) and treat all the rest (294, including
the 6 without a region) as "non-US" so none is skipped by a batch or a test.

#### `web/data/plans.json` rows may share an `id` - one row per depicted site, per-site url
Where: `web/data/plans.json`, `web/index.html` (`P.byId`), `tools/export_plans.py`, test row lookups
Symptom: code that resolves a plan by id through a dict gets the wrong site's row: two rows share
the id (one per depicted site) and carry a DIFFERENT url/media path per site, so `rows_by_id[plan]`
returns site A's row when the entry belongs to site B (hit by tests/test_batch_eu.py, which then
asserted the stonehenge url against the avebury entry). The true key is `(id, sites[0])`; look up a
row per site from the site's own candidate list. As of the plan two pairs share an id: "The new
Larned History..." (avebury-q661855 + stonehenge-q39671) and "File:Mayburgh-1769.png"
(mayburgh-henge + king-arthur-s-round-table). The page's `P.byId` keeps only the last of the shared-
`id` rows; the fit-tool keying fix is scoped into 201.

#### `serve.py` runs the plan_fit sync only after a platefits write, never at startup
Where: `server/serve.py` (`after_write`), `pipeline/plan_fit.py`
Symptom: (a safety fact, not an error) a GET-only test server never rebuilds site overlays; a
PUT/DELETE to `/api/db/platefits/*` wakes a worker thread that runs `plan_fit.main()` (it syncs all fits)
and the page polls `depictions.json` for the result.
Why: `after_write()` wakes the worker only for the `platefits` collection (its comment records that a
subprocess launched from the server silently died). GET-only tests are therefore safe and offline; a test
that PUTs a platefit should poll the site's `depictions.json`, not run `plan_fit` itself.

#### Composing a rotated/scaled Web-Mercator similarity about a centroid needs the full `a*w + b`, not just `a`
Where: `pipeline/plan_fit.py` (`similarity`), `pipeline/fit_gate.py` (`placement`), anything that derives a
wrong-placement variant of a fit (spike 7, `tools/gate_heldout.py`)
Symptom: a 10 deg turn or 15% scale about the placement centroid built as (a', b') =
(s*e^(iθ)*a, (1 - s*e^(iθ))*C_m) puts every anchor kilometres away (residuals ~4e6 m, gate kills the case
for the wrong reason, and a per-case pattern like the 0.1745 rot10 slope floor no longer appears).
Why: T'(w) = C + s*e^(iθ)*(T(w) - C) expands to s*e^(iθ)*T(w) + (1 - s*e^(iθ))*C, so b' must carry the
transformed b, b' = s*e^(iθ)*b + (1 - s*e^(iθ))*C_m (C_m = C/k in Mercator metres; C the placement's ground
centroid). The short form is only right when b = 0 (anchor centroid at the origin). The five verified
recipes (they reproduce docs/gate.md section 5 exactly): true (a, b); moved (a, b + d/k); rot10
(e^(i10°)*a, e^(i10°)*b + (1 - e^(i10°))*C_m); scale15 (1.15*a, 1.15*b - 0.15*C_m); xsite (a, b + (C_next - C)/k).

#### fit_gate cannot reject a 15% scale error at n = 3-6 anchors - a structural limit, not a bug
Where: `pipeline/fit_gate.py`, `tools/gate_heldout.py`, `docs/gate.md` sections 7 and 9
Symptom: the gate ACCEPTS scale15 placements: dev 2/12 (castle-rising, whitley), held-out 4/8
(avebury, badbury-rings, camp-d-attila, old-sarum n0142) - slope_o 0.130-0.144, all under the
frozen 0.145, none deep enough for the io < -10 clause.
Why: the theoretical 0.15*rho slope is attenuated by anchor noise in a through-origin fit at
n = 3-6 (dev band 0.130-0.141, held-out band 0.131-0.144 - the same band on both sets, so it
is not a threshold accident), and the residual pattern of a 15% scale sits inside a true
fit's own scatter: no pure-geometry statistic of these anchors can tell them apart. Do not
re-tune on the dev/held-out documents (the registration in docs/gate.md section 1 is void if
the frozen constants change) and do not add a scale-specific clause trained on this data.
Accept the 1-in-8 scale-error acceptance, backstopped by the review queue (GOAL 1) and the
human's 18/20 sample of auto-accepted fits (GOAL 3); a tighter rule may only be derived on
fresh documents with a fresh seed.

#### In-place re-dump of a jsonl line must carry the line terminator or rows glue together
Where: `fit/evidence.py` (`set_field`, `rewrite`, `record`); the test that guards it: `tests/test_evidence.py` (`test_record_appends_evidence_without_touching_existing_bytes`)
Symptom: after a `record`-style rewrite, one line of a jsonl file contains two JSON objects (this line
plus the next), the line count looks normal, and parsing the line as one object fails.
Why: `json.dumps` never emits a trailing newline, and a writer that replaces whole lines (readlines +
writelines) glues the next row onto the re-dumped one. `set_field` now appends `"\n"` iff the input line
had one. Any new in-place re-dump of a line-oriented file must do the same; verify with a per-line
parse + line-count + terminator check after the write.

#### The book matcher injects the book's default state and ties rows by token / exact-phrase lookup, never by full-name substring
Where: `pipeline/books_match.py` (`BOOK_SCOPE`, `row_inputs`, `score_candidate`, `match_row`), `fit/evidence.py` (`check_book_caption`)
Symptom: a re-verification of the matcher's own stored decisions FAILs matched rows with "stored place
state='ohio' recomputes to None" or "the row does not name 'Small multivallate hillfort on Pulpit Hill'"
(52 of the 135 matched book rows, found when 200 ran check on the real index).
Why: `match_row`'s place includes the BOOK_SCOPE default state (lapham_1855 wisconsin; fowke_1902 /
whittlesey_1850 / mills_1914 ohio; squier_1851 new york) when the printed text names none, and it ties a
row to a site by distinctive-token sharing or an exact phrase/alias lookup - the site's full name is
rarely printed (a title printing "Pulpit Hill" ties the site whose name is "Small multivallate hillfort on
Pulpit Hill"). Any consumer that re-verifies matcher decisions must call the matcher's own extracted
rules (`row_inputs` + `score_candidate`), never a stricter restatement of them.

#### The matcher's full output is non-monotone in catalog growth - never golden-pin it against the growing files
Where: `pipeline/books_match.py` (`main`, `match_row`), `data/books/matches.jsonl` (tracked), tasks 204-211 (they grow `data/books/index.jsonl` and the catalog)
Symptom: a persistent golden over `matches.jsonl` or the per-book status counts breaks when another task

Why: the margin is a property of the whole candidate pool, not of one pair. To prove a matcher refactor
behavior-neutral, do a one-off before/after run and byte-compare (`matches.jsonl` hash + printed summary),
as 200 did. The evidence check deliberately stores the runner-up margin and does not re-run the matcher
over the catalog.

#### The catalog castrum-levefanum-q1309559 is the DUTCH Limes fort (5.35E 51.96N), not Beauvais (1.99E 49.42N)
Where: `data/catalog/sites.jsonl` (castrum-levefanum-q1309559); every distance computation or site identification

Why: the name does not carry the geography - the catalog records the Dutch identification of the Roman
      Levefanum/Casaromago printed on the Peutinger map. Use the catalog's stored lon/lat, never a guess from

#### stage() staging files are append-only and idempotent on (site, title) - a changed id rule leaves the old rows behind
Where: `stage()` in `fit/src_van_deventer.py` / `fit/src_artists.py` (the per-source staging
      `extras_*.jsonl` / `files_*.jsonl` / `classified_*.jsonl`)
Symptom: after a re-stage where the site-id rule changed (e.g. an inline slug replaced by `catalog.slug`,
      "chi-vres" -> "chievres"), the files hold a row per town under the OLD id plus a second row with the
      same title under the NEW id - the (old_sid, title) pair is already in `have`, so the old row is never
      rewritten or dropped.
Why: stage() appends, and idempotency is per (site, title) pair; a changed id is a new pair. The staging
      files are the task's own and are consolidated by 211 later, so when the id key changes before 211
      runs: delete the three staging files and re-run `stage` (the files then hold one id generation only).

### Wikimedia APIs (Commons, Wikidata)

#### A Commons file page's structured data is a local MediaInfo item (M<page id>), not a global Wikidata item
Where: `fit/evidence.py` (`fetch_page_ids`, `fetch_file_entities`); the Commons API `w/api.php`; any future
      per-file metadata fetching (task 801, and the batch tasks that harvest file pages)
Symptom: searching a file page's HTML for its Wikidata item id (`ItemPage/(Q\d+)`, `"wikibaseItem"`,
      `"globalItem"`) finds nothing (or finds unrelated items: Q13414952 is MD5 - it appears as a P459
      qualifier on the file's content-hash statement; Q19652 is "public domain" - the P6216 license). The
      page's `mw.config` carries `"wbEntityId":"M<page id>"` instead.
Why: files uploaded without a global Wikidata item get a *local* Wikibase entity on Commons (the
      wbmi/"MediaInfo" integration), and its statements are what the file page's "Structured data" tab
      shows. The local wiki's `wbgetentities` answers `ids=M<page id>` directly (the `site` parameter is
      rejected with a warning but not needed; the entity comes back under `"statements"`, not the WD
      service's `"claims"`), and a page that does have a global item answers with `{"missing":"true",
      "normalized":{"item":"Q…"}}` - chase that Q id through the Wikidata service for the real claims.
      Batch 50 ids per call, pace with `commons.get` (1 s).

#### P6216 is the license property, never a depicts claim - do not group it with P180
Where: `fit/evidence.py` (`fetch_file_entities`, `check_depicts`); any regex or dict over wbmi/Wikidata
      statements that treats property lists loosely
Symptom: a statement matcher over the file item that accepts "P180|P6216" as depictions reports
      "public domain" (Q19652) or other license items as depicted entities - a false depiction tie.
Why: MediaInfo items always carry a P6216 (license) statement, so any P180|P6216 alternation is
      guaranteed to pick up licenses. Only P180 (depicts) is a depiction; the site-side depiction
      evidence is P3311 (plan) / P18 (image) on the site's item.

#### The Latin Peutinger names (Casaromago, Sammarobriva) have no Wikidata item; "Peutinger" resolves to a German gymnasium
Where: `fit/evidence.py` (`resolve_places`, the sheet candidate walk, task 801); the Wikidata `wbsearchentities`
Symptom: a search for "Casaromago" or "Sammarobriva" (the Roman names printed on the Dutch Limes sheets) returns
      [] - no place resolution; a search for "Peutinger" returns Q2081791 (Peutinger-Gymnasium Ellwangen,
      10.13E 48.97N) as its first hit, 475-500 km from both Dutch Limes sites.
Why: the Peutinger map's Latin place names were never itemized, and the one surviving "Peutinger" item is the
      gymnasium named after the map's owner. A first-resolved walk over such rows lands on that far item and
      records a conflict (the rows stay `none` with the conflict stored) - never a false pass; if a Latin name
      ever gets an item, the walk picks it up automatically.

#### `commons.members()` returns namespaced titles; subcats need `split(":",1)[1]`, file members must NOT be stripped
Where: `pipeline/commons.py:members`, `fit/src_kip.py:list_files`; any code comparing live category members against
      stored names
Symptom: comparing live subcategory members against bare names ("Britannia Illustrata") fails every comparison -
      the API returns `"Category:Britannia Illustrata"` for subcats but `"File:..."` for files; a drift assert
      comparing the two kinds of titles dies on the first category.
Why: the Commons API `members` call returns the page titles exactly as stored: subcategory pages carry the
      `Category:` prefix, file pages the `File:` prefix. Strip the prefix only for subcats (`split(":",1)[1]`);
      file titles keep `File:` everywhere downstream (inventory keys, staging rows, the `evidence` field) -
      stripping there would desynchronize them from `sources.py` and the canonical rows.

#### The Commons `DateTimeOriginal` (`date` in `commons.info()`) is not always the original's date
Where: `pipeline/commons.py:info()` (the `date` key = extmetadata `DateTimeOriginal`); every consumer that
      records a drawing's age from it (staged file rows, the date column of `docs/lead_kip.md` §3)
Symptom: a scanned print's "date" comes back as a publication sentence ("Published in Reistogt naar en door
      Oostindien, Amsterdam, c. 1775"), an upload date ("5 December 2005 (original upload date)"), or the date
      of a PHOTO of the print (2016-10-26 for a 2016 scan of a 1707 plate) - not the plate's own date.
Why: curators fill DateTimeOriginal inconsistently: for photos it is the shooting date, for book scans often
      the publication's date, sometimes free text. Before using the field to record a plate's age, check what
      the file is (plate scan / photo / book page): the plate's date usually sits in the TITLE or in the
      Rijks-style `Titel(s):` line of the description (the `desc` field), and `stage()` should take it from
      there.

#### From this VM, `iiprop=wbentity` returns nothing for ANY file - the depicts/M-item route is unusable
Where: the Commons API `iiprop=wbentity` (a file -> its MediaInfo item); the planned P180 (depicts) evidence

Symptom: the response has no `item` for every file tried: the Gott 112a Temple Newsam scan, the Rijksmuseum

Why: the mechanism yields nothing from this VM (server-side gating, or the parameter is not served here); it

#### The en.wikipedia API: `action=query` and `action=parse` own disjoint property sets; a missing page is `missing:""` in query, `missingtitle` in parse
Where: `https://en.wikipedia.org/w/api.php` (via `commons.get`, which sets the UA); task 205's infobox checks
      (Kings Weston House, pageid 10102492)
Symptom: `action=parse&prop=coordinates` errors (coordinates is a query prop); `action=query&prop=wikitext`
      errors (wikitext is a parse prop); an absent page under `action=query&titles=` comes back as a page object
      with `"missing":""` - an EMPTY STRING, falsy, so `if page.get("missing")` reads as "present". Under
      `action=parse` the same page gives `"missingtitle":"true"`.
Why: two actions, disjoint prop namespaces; the query missing-marker is the empty string. Test for
      `"missing" in page`. Get the infobox coordinates from `action=query&prop=coordinates` and the article body
      from `action=parse&prop=wikitext` - two calls, never one.
#### wbsearchentities with limit=5 misses well-known short names - Mons (Belgium) ranks 11th in the en search
Where: `fit/src_van_deventer.py` (`_search_candidates`, the default limit 5) and any script calling the
      Wikidata wbsearchentities API for a short, common town name
Symptom: the town's item is simply absent from the five candidates (no error, just a short list) - the
      discovery run records a wrong or no QID; for 'Mons' the five were the planetary nomenclature term 'mons'
      plus French communes (Var, Hérault, Charente, Gard) while the Belgian city Q83407 was 11th (4th in the
      fr search)
Why: short common names get outranked by their many homonyms. When the expected item is not among the five,
      re-search at limit 20 (and in the other language), then re-check label + P625 + P373 + enwiki before
      recording - the 204 BE batch found Mons only this way (lead doc, QID verification - Belgium).

#### A wbsearchentities label search containing parentheses returns EMPTY
Where: the Wikidata wbsearchentities API for a label-based search (fit/src_van_deventer.py
      `_search_candidates`; task 204's 'Luxembourg (city)' lookup)
Symptom: search='Luxembourg (city)' returns [] - no candidates, no error - while the item exists and the
      unparenthesized search 'Luxembourg City' hits it (Q1842 came first at limit 20; the
      plain 'Luxembourg' search ranks the country Q32 and the Belgian province Q1126 ahead of it)
Why: the search matches labels, and '(city)' is a Wikipedia-style disambiguation that no Wikidata label
      carries (the item's label is just 'Luxembourg'). A parenthesized or otherwise qualified search term is a
      guess about a label that does not exist and silently returns nothing. Search the unparenthesized form
      (or a label form that actually exists) and let the candidate fact sheet (label + P625 + P373 + enwiki)
      do the disambiguation.

#### A Wikimedia API call with no User-Agent gets HTTP 403; commons.get already sets one, a raw script must too
Where: `pipeline/commons.py` (`get`, sets `aw.UA`) and any throwaway script hitting the Wikimedia APIs
      directly (e.g. the thumb download snippet of the 204 BE eye check)
Symptom: HTTP Error 403: Forbidden on the very first request; the same request works once a User-Agent is sent
Why: Wikimedia's robot policy rejects requests without a descriptive User-Agent. `aw.UA` is the project's
      standard value: a DICT ({"User-Agent": ...}), not a string - pass it to urllib's Request(headers=)
      as-is, but slicing it like a string (UA[:60]) raises KeyError. A raw urllib script must set it (or go
      through `commons.get`, which paces and retries too).

### fit/

#### Python binds `/` and `%` at the same precedence (left-associative), and `or` binds below both
Where: `fit/batch_us.py` (`write_report`, path building), `tests/test_batch_us.py`
      (`_check_doc`, `_check_doc_stub`)
Symptom: `Path(root) / "a" / "%s.json" % (x, y)` raises `TypeError: unsupported operand type(s)
      for %: 'PosixPath' and 'tuple'` - the expression parses as `(Path(root) / "a" / "%s.json") %
      (x, y)`. Likewise `"a" or "b" / "c"` parses as `"a" or ("b" / "c")` (one silent wrong-value
      hit and one crash in the batch work).
Why: in Python's precedence table `* / // %` form one level, `+ -` the next, then comparisons,
      then `not` / `and` / `or`. So a `%` formatting applied to a path string is swallowed into the
      `/` chain before it, and a `/` into an `or`. Always parenthesize a format string inside a
      chain: `Path(root) / ("a%s.json" % (x, y))`; never mix `/` with `or` unparenthesized.

#### `batch_us.pre_docs` matches any existing `<site>.*.json` document - including automatic docs the current run just wrote
Where: `fit/batch_us.py` (`pre_docs`, `run_sites`), `tests/test_batch_us.py`
Symptom: code that computes a site's "pre-batch" state AFTER `run_sites` treats every candidate as
      already pre-fit: for serpent-mound the expected set comes out empty and an assertion compares
      15 new automatic documents against `set()` - which looks like a gate-verdict mismatch, but
      the gate (pipeline/fit_gate.py) is a pure function of (pairs, transform) plus frozen module
      constants, so two identical calls cannot disagree.
Why: `pre_docs` scans data/db/platefits/ as it stands at call time, and the batch writes its
      automatic documents into that same directory during the run. Snapshot the pre-run state
      (`pre_docs`, `is_pre_fit`) BEFORE calling `run_sites`; compare the post-run directory only for
      "what is new". (Session-3 misdiagnosis: it first read as cross-test state pollution.)

#### Recorded-answer batch tests must be state-aware: an earlier run's auto docs are pre-docs for the next run's recorded model
Where: `tests/test_batch_eu.py` (`test_hand_fitted_sites_get_items_for_their_other_pictures`),
      `fit/batch_us.py` (`run_sites`'s skip rule), `fit/batch_eu.py`
Symptom: a test that pins an item's expected candidates against the full candidate list passes on
      the pre-run tree and fails after the working run ("Extra items in the right set: c_..."): the
      plans the run turned into automatic documents are skipped as pre-docs by the test's recorded
      run (never re-fitted, no entry) and never appear in the item.
Why: `run_sites` skips any candidate whose doc exists at call time (`have = pre_docs ∪ docs written
      this run`), and the test's temp tree copy carries the previous run's documents. Expectations
      computed from a static list of candidate ids go stale the moment any run adds a document -
      this also hits 212's re-coverage run, which adds docs for grown sites.
Do this instead: compute expectations from the live tree state at test time: fresh = candidates
      minus `pre_docs` (re-read in the test, never a constant), expected item candidates = the live
      item's candidates (a working run may have left one) ∪ fresh (exact equality), and assert the
      post-run invariants (one file per site, named after candidates[0].plan; resolved unchanged).
      The test then passes before and after every run.

#### `data/db/platefits/` mixes hand fits and automatic ones (`"auto": true`) - code that counts the directory's files must filter `doc.get("auto")`
Where: `tools/gate_heldout.py` (`partition`), `fit/batch_us.py` (`write_doc`, `write_golden`), `data/db/platefits/`
Symptom: code that treats every `data/db/platefits/*.json` as a hand-fit reference breaks once a batch
      lands: after 203a's US batch the directory holds 36 documents (20 hand + 16 auto), and the
      pre-802 `gate_heldout partition()` aborted with "expected 20 hand-fit documents in
      data/db/platefits/, found 36; the registered partition is void" (the suite's red test_gate).
Why: the batch writes its accepted fits into that same directory (`write_doc`), but the
      golden/held-out reference is the 20 hand fits, which 203a's golden pins byte-identical after
      the run. Count or list the NON-automatic set: `if not json.load(open(p)).get("auto")`
      (the `write_golden` criterion; a doc without the field is a hand fit). Automatic documents
      only ever ADD names - a hand-fit doc never gains the field - so any derivation over the
      non-auto name list is state-agnostic: identical before and after a batch, and a hand-fit doc
      that did gain the field drops the count below 20 and fails loudly (correct: the reference
      was changed).

#### The one-shot gate registration is frozen at exactly 20 named hand-fit docs - a 21st hand doc (a post-registration hand fit) trips gate_heldout's "expected 20" precondition; the fix is owned by task 218, don't work around it
Where: `tools/gate_heldout.py` (`partition`, `REGISTERED`), `data/db/platefits/`, `tests/test_gate.py::test_recorded_measurement_reproduces_and_agrees`, docs/gate.md sections 1 and 3
Symptom: "gate_heldout: expected 20 hand-fit documents in data/db/platefits/, found 21; the
      registered partition is void, see docs/gate.md section 1" - appears on the full suite once a
      hand-fit doc added after the registration (206's shotwick-castle-q7502621; then 207a/b/c's
      Roman hand fits) lands in the directory
Why: 802 excluded the auto docs from the count, but the precondition `len(names) != 20` still
      counts every hand doc: the registration names the 20, it does not say "whatever is in the
      directory". When you hit this (a branch carrying a post-registration hand doc), the failing
      test is owned by 218 - do not rename or delete the hand doc, do not touch the REGISTERED
      list, tests/golden/gate_heldout.txt or docs/gate.md, and do not loosen the test; add 218 to
      your own `Depends on:` and wait for it to merge (the driver resyncs the branch).

#### This Qwen fabricates correspondences that pass a consistency-only gate; the batch's prompt/parse/scale/texture checks are the counterweight
Where: `fit/batch_us.py` (`llm_model`, `_model_prompt`, `_parse_answer`, `_feature_present`), the local qwen3.8-27b via
      `pipeline/llm.py`, docs/gate.md section 7
Symptom: asked to match features between two gridded panels, the model answers with internally
      perfect but false correspondences (identity (100,100)->(100,100)..., the four corners to the
      four corners, a 5-point diagonal ladder, a 1:1 pixel line ~281 m off the 202 seed): gate med
      ~0.0 m, and the frozen gate ACCEPTS them - docs/gate.md section 7: a consistency check cannot
      see a consistent global error. Unopposed, every automatic batch document would be garbage and
      the human's 18/20 report-sample check would fail.
Why: a 27 B vision model that cannot confidently read a figure (e.g. a small figure on a dense
      text page) invents a regular grid-like correspondence instead of reporting few pairs. The
      gate is frozen, so the counterweight is batch-side: a prompt giving both panels' labelled
      coordinate ranges + metre coverage, a +/-50% seed-scale window, anti-pattern clauses (no
      grid-line intersections / even spacing / >=3 collinear; never pad a list) and asking for
      named features plus a stated scale; parsing drops pairs outside the labelled ranges; a
      stated scale that disagrees >=2x with the MAGNITUDE of the model's own points' similarity
      trims the answer to 3 pairs (a review item, never an automatic document); and a
      feature-presence check (`_feature_present`) trims an answer whose ground points mostly sit
      on less textured ground than the median of a 400-point null of the site's own image. The
      last one is needed for a fifth class the other checks all pass (4c pilot, tremper): a
      correct-scale, wrong-translation answer whose points sit on structureless ground. The
      checks only ever route to review; a fabrication anchored on strong texture (roads, field
      boundaries) passes all of them - docs/gate.md section 7's human 18/20 sample is the
      backstop for that class.

#### 201's upsert merges item candidates by whole-entry replacement per plan - a subset-shaped entry drops the denormalized row fields; the page's row lookup, not the entry, covers the save flow
Where: `fit/review.py` (`upsert_item`), `fit/batch_us.py` (`write_item`), `data/review/*.json`,
      `web/review.js` (`rvResolveRow`), `web/index.html` (`openPlan`), `tests/test_review.py`
      (`test_save_resolves_the_item`)
Symptom: after a consumer upserts a candidate whose entry lacks the page-save fields, code that
      reads them from the ITEM ENTRY fails with KeyError: the 203a batch's entry shape (plan,
      title, url, evidence, pairs, coarse, ground, scale_m_px, rot_deg, scale_source, note,
      why, gate_score) replaced the 201-seed entry for alligator's n0214_2 (which also stored
      map_box, size, ia, file, label, book, cite, view), and the test died with
      `KeyError: 'map_box'`. The page itself never misbehaved.
Why: `upsert_item`'s documented merge is "a same-plan entry replaces the existing one in
      place" - fields absent from the incoming entry are simply gone. But the page does not
      rely on the stored copies: `rvResolveRow` resolves the candidate's row from
      web/data/plans.json by (plan, site) FIRST, and the stored-field fallback (missing
      map_box tolerated, `openPlan` falls back to the full frame) exists only for rows absent
      from the current build. Read those fields from the plans.json ROW (map_box, size, ia,
      file, label, book, cite, view are all row columns) - never from an item's entry, which
      any later upsert may have re-shaped.

#### `batch_us.write_report(path=None)` silently falls back to `docs/batch_us.md` - a reuser must pin its own default before calling
Where: `fit/batch_us.py` (`write_report`: `out = Path(root) / (path or "docs/batch_us.md")`),
      `fit/batch_eu.py` (`write_report`, which pins `path or "docs/batch_eu.md"`)
Symptom: a second batch passing `path=None` writes (and in a hard-linked test tree, overwrites
      in place) the US batch's report file instead of its own - the content says "The batch, EU
      (203b)" but the path says batch_us.md.
Why: the writer's default path is the US report's name, and 203b's thin wrapper initially
      forwarded `None` straight through (caught in the first dry run). Any module that reuses
      `batch_us.write_report` for a different file must supply a non-None default itself. Also:
      its `at` parameter is vestigial - the body never uses it, so the report's determinism does
      not depend on it.

### pipeline/

#### `llm.ask`'s default `url=URL` binds at def time - reassigning `llm.URL` after import does nothing
Where: `pipeline/llm.py` (`URL = os.environ.get("AW_LLM_URL", "http://127.0.0.1:18080/...")` read
      once at module level; `ask(prompt, images=(), ..., url=URL)`) and any caller that imports it
      (`fit/batch_us.py`'s `llm_model`)
Symptom: after `import llm; llm.URL = "http://127.0.0.1:8081/..."` the requests still go to the
      module default (18080 on this machine, where nothing listens; the AI-box tunnel serves
      8080/8081 vLLM and 8082 llama.cpp) - a confusing connection error instead of a visible
      wrong-URL error.
Why: default arguments capture the value at function-definition time, not the module attribute at
      call time. Set `AW_LLM_URL` in the environment BEFORE the import (read once, at module level)
or pass `url=` explicitly to `ask`/`ask_json`.
#### Q50195 (Imola) P625 is the correct city point - the prep's "old-town centre" was Cervia; never geocode Imola from OSM/Nominatim; "Venice" search hits Venice, California, first
Where: `fit/src_artists.py` (SITES, `verify_qids`, task 213); `fit/evidence.py` (`resolve_places`, `caption_route`); OSM/Nominatim geocoding of Imola
Symptom: a prep-era "old-town centre" (44.245 N, 12.367 E) was called Imola's, and Q50195's P625 (44.3531,
      11.7147) was called "bad, ~53 km NW of the town" - in fact the prep point is CERVIA on the Ravenna coast
      (~50 km SE of Imola) and the P625 is the correct city point (the enwiki infobox 44 deg 21' 11" N 11 deg
      42' 53" E agrees with it to 0.3 km, and the OSM town node with the F1 circuit beside it sits there too).
      OSM/Nominatim geocoding of "Imola" is a second trap: the comune boundary is mis-drawn (Nominatim shows the
      urban area as "Imola, Nuovo Circondario Imolese"; the boundary's centroid sits ~8 km north of the city).
      Separately, a name search for "Venice" first returns Q773853 (Venice, Los Angeles area, -118.46, 33.99),
      9891 km -> a live `record` stores that as a conflict (kind `none`) for rows captioning Venice.
Why: for Imola the live record route resolves the RIGHT QID, but the site point is the sheet's own centre -
      the walled old town (Piazza del Duomo 11.7112, 44.3535, OSM), where the view is centred - not the modern
      city point; 213 hand-records `caption_coords` with that point as both site and place (the offline check
      passes). For Venice the stored point is the item's own P625 (sane). Also: Q16139 is the Province of
      Bologna, NOT Italy (the prep notes misread it; Italy is Q38) - P131 gives provinces, so the staged extras
      `place` strings are composed by hand (region, country).

#### Nominatim's viewbox is left,top,right,bottom = min_lon,MAX_lat,max_lon,min_lat
Where: Nominatim (nominatim.openstreetmap.org) `viewbox` parameter; any OSM-geocoding helper that wants to bias results to a region
Symptom: passing the bounding box as (lon1, lat1, lon2, lat2) makes Nominatim re-rank results toward the centre
      of a mis-specified box, so the intended region's results get buried (a 213 search for the right place came
      back ordered toward the wrong corner).
Why: the documented format is "viewbox=min_lon,max_lat,max_lon,min_lat" (left,top,right,bottom). Build it as
      f"{min_lon},{max_lat},{max_lon},{min_lat}". (Burned a 213 session on this, 2026-10-11.)

#### The Wikimedia APIs 429 after ~12-20 back-to-back calls even at 1-2 s pacing; commons.get's Retry-After handling absorbs it
Where: `pipeline/commons.py` (`get`, `PACE_S = 1.0`); `pipeline/plan_fit.py` (`_fetch`, same pacing -
      added 2026-10-11 by task 300 after its bare-urllib `load_picture` was the one unpaced live fetcher);
      every live-fetching module (fit/evidence.py record,
      fit/src_van_deventer.py --list/--verify/--files/--chain)
Symptom: HTTP 429 from commons.wikimedia.org or wikidata.org `w/api.php` after a dozen or so consecutive
      calls, even when paced 1-2 s apart
Why: Wikimedia rate-limits per-client bursts well below 1 req/s in practice. `commons.get()` is
      Retry-After-aware (it sleeps the server's value and retries) - use it (or replicate its pacing) instead
      of a bare urllib call with a fixed sleep; a 26-call verify run completed in ~30 s wall on 2026-10-11
      with no manual intervention. Never loop a hand-rolled fetcher without the Retry-After handling.

#### A platefit doc's `size` is the browser image's size, not the big cache file's - `m_per_px` in depictions.json depends on the big image's dimensions
Where: `pipeline/plan_fit.py` (`load_picture`, `similarity`, `build`); `data/db/platefits/*.json`
      (`size`, `crop`, `pairs`); `web/data/sites/*/depictions.json` (`fit.m_per_px`)
Symptom: re-running plan_fit.build on a stand-in picture sized like `doc["size"]` writes a depictions entry
      whose `m_per_px` differs from the stored one (for stonehenge's 7 docs, 3 of the big cache files are
      1.19-1.75x the doc size: c_098c4cb138676939's stored m_per_px 0.6686 becomes 0.5622 at fs=1), while
      every other field (corners, resid_m, rot_deg, source line) is unchanged.
Why: the page's plate tool places `pairs`/`crop` in the displayed image's pixels (`doc["size"]`), and the
      overlay is built from a bigger rendering of the same file: `load_picture` returns `fs =
      big.width/size[0]`, and solving the similarity on the scaled pairs divides m_per_px by fs. The pixels
      never enter the fit at all (pure least squares over the point pairs), so a stand-in image at the
      EXACT big-image dimensions (read from the cache file's PIL header) reproduces depictions.json
      byte-for-byte with any pixel content (flat colour is fine); one sized like `doc["size"]` (fs=1) does
      not. That is how tests/test_site_done.py stays network-free and byte-exact (task 300).

### fit/evidence.py (the evidence contract)

#### check_category re-verifies only the chain's SHAPE - the walk itself is the verification
Where: `fit/evidence.py` (`check_category`); every module that records `kind: category` evidence
      (fit/src_van_deventer.py's cat_chain -> TOWNS["chain"] -> evidence_for)
Symptom: nothing fails: a hand-typed or transformed "via" (a " -> "-joined string, a list that includes the
      file's own category, a chain that skips a hop) passes the offline check, and a picture ends up tied to
      the wrong place
Why: `check_category` only asserts row.cat == site_cat, via[-1] == cat, file_cat not in via - it cannot
      re-walk Commons offline. Record ONLY the actually walked parent list (the JSON a chain walker prints),
      with via[-1] == the site's exact P373 string and the file's category absent from it; a failed walk is
      the caption route or a documented drop, never a guessed chain.

### pipeline/commons.py

#### keep() must be judged AFTER the date/date_commons swap - a post-1925 reproduction of a pre-1925 drawing is dropped otherwise
Where: `pipeline/commons.py` (`keep`, `year_of`, `MAX_YEAR`); `pipeline/sources.py` (`run` - the correct
      order: swap, then gate); `fit/src_van_deventer.py` (`stage` - had the wrong order, fixed 2026-10-11)
Symptom: a staging run raises on a reproduction: "commons.keep() would drop 'File:Plattegrond van J. van
      Deventer, reproductie uit album ... - Sluis - 20201361 - RCE.jpg': fix the table or record the drop" -
      although the byte-same Zwolle done row sits in the canonical files.jsonl (date "circa 1560",
      date_commons "1980")
Why: keep() judges via year_of(title, m), which reads m["date"] (the page/scan date) first. A scan whose page
      date is post-1925 but whose subject is a pre-1925 drawing must be passed the known drawing date FIRST
      (date=want, date_commons=the page value) - sources.py's run() swaps and only then calls keep(), so the
      drawing's year (1560) is what gets judged, not the scan's (1980 > 1925). The done Zwolle row (a 1980 RCE
      album reproduction of a c. 1560 drawing) is the template; any staging module that gates before swapping
      silently drops exactly those reproductions.

### pipeline/books.py, pipeline/books_ia.py (the book machinery)

#### civitatesorbiste00brau's hOCR page index is misaligned with the jp2 leaf sequence - page_texts is unreliable for this book
Where: `pipeline/books_ia.py` (`page_texts`, `djvu_txt`, `ocr_captions`) for IA id civitatesorbiste00brau (Civitates Orbis Terrarum, Liber secundus, 1575); `data/books/triage/civitatesorbiste00brau.A.jsonl`; task 217
Symptom: the hOCR leaf 85 text holds the Brussels title that stage A reads on leaf 87; the drift is not constant - it runs 0-2 leaves down the book (leaf 53 matches, leaf 109 is off by two) - so text looked up through the page index lands on the wrong leaf.
Why: this BookReader scan's hOCR stream and jp2 leaf sequence do not line up. The image-based stage A rows (read from the leaf image) are the ground truth for this book; 217's view-as-drawing index must key on leaf n, never on the hOCR page index.

#### The civitates A/F "plan" labels are unreliable in both directions - the hand list's kind is the only source
Where: `pipeline/books.py` stage A/F prompts, `data/books/triage/civitatesorbiste00brau.{A,F}.jsonl`, `data/books/lists/civitatesorbiste00brau.json`; tasks 216/217
Symptom: F flags 11 of the 121 figure pages as containing a "plan", but of F's ten distinct plan leaves (A30, 62, 65, 66, 90, 93, 105, 186, 229x2, 237) only A90 (Ghent) and A237 (Jerusalem old) are true plans - it misses the five famous plans (A58 Paris, A85 Brussels, A98 Antwerp, A109 Amsterdam, A238 Jerusalem new) and false-flags A186 (the Augsburg view); stage A typed only 3 of 121 figure leaves as plate_site_plan (A187/A199 are blank fold-out versos).
Why: both prompts are biased toward earthwork survey plans, not engraved bird's-eye plans. The hand list's `kind` field (7 plans, kind_by "hand") is the only source for plan calls on this book. The same view-plate bias applies to the other five untriaged civitates/Merian volumes (ARes73114, ARes73115, 17095748888888bsb-00105587, topographiahelve00zeil, rcin.org.pl.WA51_13719_PANB665-r1642_Topographia-Helvetia_152915).

#### Roy, Military Antiquities of the Romans in North Britain (1793), is not on the Internet Archive
Where: task 207c; IA advancedsearch (exact title, creator, full-text phrases, 1790-1800 year range, ten guessed identifier patterns); the only related IA item macdonald-1917-roy (a 1917 dissertation about Roy)
Symptom: no IA copy of the book under any searched title/creator/phrase; ten guessed identifiers (militaryantiquit00roy*) all return {}.
Why: the 1793 Society of Antiquaries folio (174 text pages + 51 map plates) was never scanned by a library that uploads to IA. The complete online facsimile is NLS (maps.nls.uk/roy/antiquities/), which is WAF-blocked from this VM. A human-provided copy in data/raw/books/roy1793/ is the only route (207c blocked on it, open ask_human).
